purpose: Authoritative-vendor manufacturing integration delta. Adds Aspen InfoPlus.21, Yokogawa Exaquantum and Emerson DeltaV Edge Environment as distinct industrial data targets, reusing existing REST/database and OPC UA read profiles. Evidence remains specification/public-documentation level only: no sandbox or customer tenant credentials were used and all writes/control operations remain disabled.

systems.name: AspenTech Aspen InfoPlus.21 (IP.21)
systems.evidenceNote: AspenTech's current product documentation describes IP.21 as a real-time industrial historian for continuous and batch process data and documents standard integration interfaces including REST services and ODBC. It can ingest data from DCS/SCADA/PLC, ERP, MES, LIMS and third-party applications; batch/event context is available through Production Record Manager where deployed. The platform also exposes write-capable interfaces, so Manufacturing WFM reuses only the existing REST/database read profiles behind the customer edge and does not infer control authority. No IP.21 environment was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: customer-authorised IP.21 identity limited to required tags, records, events and asset/production context
REST GET/read operations and/or ODBC read-only views only
no historian configuration, tag/manual-input writes, calculation changes or process/control writes
customer-edge routing for on-prem or plant-adjacent deployments
separate source-system authority retained for workforce, payroll and production master data
dataAvailableOrExpected: continuous industrial time-series and historical tag values
timestamps, units and tag/process metadata exposed by the selected interface
calculated KPI/SPC/SQC/OEE outputs where the customer has configured them
event and batch-production context where Production Record Manager is deployed
context from DCS, SCADA, PLC, ERP, MES, LIMS and other sources already historized by the customer
automationOpportunities: correlate staffed time and labour cost with real production state, throughput and sustained downtime
use historical stop/recovery patterns to improve labour-demand and redeployment recommendations
coordinate specialist staffing with maintenance or process windows represented in historian/event context
reuse an existing enterprise historian rather than deploy duplicate direct machine integrations
detect tag/schema/version drift and distinguish raw observations from calculated or aggregated values before workforce decisions
consider any historian-side write only after a separately authorised sandbox/site write-read-back safety case
savingsHypotheses: reduce duplicate OT integration engineering by reusing IP.21 as the governed historian layer
reduce paid idle labour during recurring process stoppages and slow recoveries
reduce overtime by forecasting specialist coverage from historical production and maintenance patterns
extend WFM optimisation to mature process plants without replacing the historian
dataGaps: worker identity, employment, absence, pay and qualification truth normally remains outside IP.21
tag names, custom records, asset structure, calculations and batch models are customer-specific
exact REST/ODBC authentication and enabled interfaces vary by deployed version and customer architecture
calculated, aggregated or derived historian values must not be treated as raw live observations
historian collection quality does not prove upstream sensor or control-system correctness
constraintsRisks: many IP.21 estates are on-prem or plant-adjacent and require customer-edge routing rather than direct cloud access
REST and database interfaces may expose more than the minimum WFM dataset and must be scoped to read-only objects/views
large history queries need bounded windows, backpressure, deterministic checkpoints and retry controls
custom records and batch/event models require customer-specific canonical mapping
timestamps, quality, calculation provenance and aggregation windows must be preserved before real-time WFM automation
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST and database-read profiles for a thin IP.21 adapter with deployed-version/capability discovery, customer-edge enforcement, bounded history reads, tag/record schema fingerprints, source-time/quality/derived-value provenance and customer work-centre mappings. Obtain customer-version interface documentation plus an authorised IP.21 lab or tenant for least-privilege authentication and read-roundtrip proof before considering any write path.

systems.name: Yokogawa Exaquantum
systems.evidenceNote: Yokogawa's current Exaquantum material describes a plant information/historian platform with dynamic plant hierarchy, current and historical process data and OPC connectivity including OPC UA. Current R3.60 information documents OPC UA A&C client support and OPC UA DA/HDA server capability; Exaquantum/Batch documents ISA-88 batch, equipment, recipe, trend and alarm context. Because OPC UA server capability can also support writes in current releases, Manufacturing WFM uses Browse/Read/Subscribe only through the customer edge. No Exaquantum environment was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: customer-authorised OPC UA identity limited to approved Exaquantum namespaces and history
alarms/conditions read access only where required for WFM disruption context
no OPC UA Write/Call, historian configuration, recipe changes or control-system writes
customer-edge routing with explicit certificate trust and no anonymous production session
dataAvailableOrExpected: plant hierarchy and tag/equipment context where exposed
OPC UA data/history and alarms/conditions in supported deployments
batch, equipment, recipe and trend context where Exaquantum/Batch is deployed
production-loss and process-performance evidence derived from the customer's historian configuration
automationOpportunities: use process and batch state to adjust labour demand to actual execution rather than plan alone
trigger labour redeployment/recovery recommendations from sustained stoppage and recovery evidence
align specialist or cleaning/changeover staffing to batch/equipment state
correlate shift staffing with batch cycle time, production loss and alarms
reuse the existing Exaquantum hierarchy instead of creating another direct DCS/PLC integration
gate all OPC UA methods/writes until separately authorised and write-roundtrip certified
savingsHypotheses: reduce idle labour while batches/equipment are blocked or recovering
reduce overstaffing during delayed batches and understaffing during recovery/changeover
reduce direct DCS/PLC connector engineering by using Exaquantum as the governed read layer
reduce overtime caused by poor visibility of late-running batches and specialist demand
dataGaps: worker identity, payroll, qualifications and roster truth remain in workforce/enterprise systems
plant hierarchy, tag naming, batch models and alarm semantics are customer-specific
exact OPC UA namespace/security configuration and history capabilities vary by Exaquantum release and site
batch product/modules may not be licensed at every site
historical or recovered data can arrive late and must not masquerade as live state
constraintsRisks: Exaquantum is plant-network-adjacent and must remain behind the customer edge
current OPC UA server capability is write-capable, so method/write permissions must be excluded technically
redundancy/history-catch-up can replay older observations after connectivity loss
certificate trust, security policy and endpoint identity must be validated; anonymous production access is prohibited
quality, source timestamp, replay age and site identity must be preserved before workforce automation
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing OPC UA edge profile for a thin Exaquantum adapter with endpoint/certificate validation, Browse/Read/Subscribe-only operation allowlists, namespace and batch/equipment mapping, source-time/quality/replay-age handling and schema fingerprints. Test late history-catch-up and redundant-source replay using fixtures, then obtain an authorised Exaquantum site/lab for least-privilege authentication and read-roundtrip evidence.

systems.name: Emerson DeltaV Edge Environment
systems.evidenceNote: Emerson's March 2026 DeltaV Edge Environment documentation describes a one-way encrypted outbound replication path from DeltaV into an enterprise/plant-network edge environment, with contextualized DeltaV configuration/data then available through REST API and OPC UA. The current data sheet documents Active Directory authentication for REST and administrator-defined OPC UA users (with optional anonymous access), TLS for the upstream HTTPS flow and deployment on enterprise or Level 3 plant networks. Manufacturing WFM treats DeltaV Edge as a data projection boundary, not as control authority; anonymous OPC UA is not accepted for production and writes/control remain disabled. No DeltaV Edge environment was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: customer-authorised Active Directory REST identity or named OPC UA user scoped to required DeltaV Edge data
REST read operations and/or OPC UA Browse/Read/Subscribe only
validated TLS/certificate trust and endpoint identity
no anonymous OPC UA for production WFM connectivity
no DeltaV DCS engineering, control, configuration or process-write authority
dataAvailableOrExpected: replicated DeltaV operational data exposed by the Edge Environment
DeltaV configuration hierarchy and contextual relationships
near-real-time process values and associated context available through REST or OPC UA
operational state suitable for analytics, alarms/visibility and shift-performance correlation where exposed
sandboxed replicated data separated from direct access to the control system
automationOpportunities: use the replicated DeltaV state to refresh staffing demand and redeployment recommendations without direct DCS access
correlate staffing, overtime and paid idle time with process state and production interruptions
use DeltaV configuration hierarchy to accelerate work-centre and site mapping during implementation
detect stale replication or edge connectivity loss before operational data drives workforce decisions
support enterprise analytics and executive labour-to-process reporting from the same governed edge projection
keep any action back toward DeltaV outside this connector and behind a separate industrial-control safety case
savingsHypotheses: reduce bespoke DCS integration engineering by consuming the vendor-supported enterprise edge projection
reduce paid idle labour through faster response to sustained process disruption
reduce overtime by improving visibility of recovery timing and specialist demand
reduce implementation mapping effort by reusing DeltaV hierarchy/context
reduce OT security overhead versus direct cloud access to the control network
dataGaps: worker identity, pay, absence, skills and roster truth remain outside DeltaV Edge
exact REST resources, OPC UA namespace and exposed DeltaV modules depend on customer configuration/version
a replicated operational value is not evidence that the underlying instrument or control state is correct
one-way upstream replication does not itself prove the downstream consumer identity is least privilege
plant-versus-enterprise placement changes routing, firewall and latency characteristics
constraintsRisks: Edge Environment can be deployed on Level 3/plant networks; WFM cloud must not bypass the customer-controlled network boundary
OPC UA may be configured for anonymous access, which is unsuitable for production WFM and must be rejected
REST/OPC UA data freshness must be measured separately from the health of the one-way upstream replication
source time, ingestion time, hierarchy identity and quality/status must be retained to distinguish stale replicated data from live state
multiple DeltaV sites/areas require deterministic site and work-centre identity mapping
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST and OPC UA edge profiles for a thin DeltaV Edge adapter with AD/OPC UA capability discovery, authenticated-only policy, certificate pin/trust validation, source/ingestion freshness watermarks, configuration-hierarchy fingerprints and customer site/work-centre mappings. Simulate upstream replication interruption and stale-edge reads, then obtain an authorised DeltaV Edge lab/site for least-privilege authentication and read-roundtrip proof.
